title: The three persons are one God, not three gods
english: How could Peter have exposed Ananias and Sapphira for embezzling from the price of the field unless he had the gift of prophecy? And how could Saint Paul have spoken of what would happen in the last days unless he too had the gift of prophecy? The Montanist said: "Then why do you not accept holy Montanus?" The Orthodox Christian said: "Because he was a false prophet who spoke nothing true." The Montanist said: "Do not blaspheme the Advocate, man." The Orthodox Christian said: "I praise and glorify the Advocate, the Spirit of truth, but I abhor Montanus as the abomination of desolation." The Montanist said: "How?" The Orthodox Christian said: "First, because he says: 'I am the Father and I am the Son and I am the Advocate.'" The Montanist said: "But you say that the Father is one, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another." The Orthodox Christian said: "If we say it, it is not trustworthy; but if the Son teaches that the Father is one and the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, is another, then it is necessary to be persuaded." The Montanist said: "Show where he teaches this." The Orthodox Christian said: "When he says: 'I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, the Spirit of truth, to be with you forever, whom the world cannot receive because it does not see him; but you know him, because he remains with you and will be in you' (John 14:16-17). When you hear 'another Advocate,' how do you not clearly understand that he is another besides the one who speaks?" The Montanist said: "If one and another and another, then three gods." The Orthodox Christian said: "God forbid." The Montanist said: "How 'God forbid'?" The Orthodox Christian said: "Because the divine Scripture unites things that have the same nature and will." The Montanist said: "God forbid." The Orthodox Christian said: "You hear the apostle Paul saying: 'In Christ Jesus there is neither slave nor free; there is neither male nor female; there is neither Greek nor Jew, but you are all one in Christ Jesus' (Galatians 3:28). And we hear Christ himself saying about the man and the woman: 'They are no longer two, but one flesh' (Matthew 19:6). If things that exist in separation are no longer two because of the sameness of will and nature, how is it possible for bodiless things to come under number and position?" The Montanist said: "Then there is not one God." The Orthodox Christian said: "One God in respect of nature, but in person the Father is one, the Son is another, and the Holy Spirit is another." The Montanist said: "Then how does the Son say: 'On that day they will know that I am in the Father and the Father is in me' (John 14:20)? And again he says: 'If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will keep him, and we will come to him and make our dwelling with him. The one who does not love me does not keep my words, and the word that I speak is not mine, but the Father's who sent me' (John 14:23-24). 'These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you; but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and remind you of all that I have said to you' (John 14:25-26)." The Orthodox Christian said: "Unwillingly you agree with the word of truth. For if you are persuaded by what has been said, you will walk straight toward the truth. You heard that he says: 'On that day you will know that I am in the Father and the Father is in me,' and he did not say: 'On that day you will all know that I am Father and Son.' And you hear that he says: 'We will come to him, I and the Father'; he did not say to him: 'I and the Father and the Son will come and make a dwelling.' But also: 'The word that I speak is not mine, but the Father's who sent me' shows nothing other than the distinctness of the persons. And when you hear: 'These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you; but the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all that I have said to you,' how will you not, blushing at yourself, confess the clear distinction of the three persons?" The Montanist said: "On the day ... of judgment the three persons will sit to judge the living and the dead." The Orthodox Christian said: "When you hear 'they will sit' in a bodily way, understand it spiritually, so that you do not suppose places and separations of bodies, but the fixedness of the nature. For the Father is everywhere, the Son is everywhere, the Holy Spirit is everywhere, and just as there is nothing between mind and word and breath, so there is nothing between Father and Son and Holy Spirit."
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The Montanist has just objected that the Orthodox speaker's distinction of Father, Son, and Spirit implies three gods; the Orthodox speaker now argues from Scripture that the three share one nature and will, and that the Son himself teaches the distinction of persons.

title: The Spirit as down payment of promised goods
english: The Orthodox Christian said: "We must understand the Father as perfect, in a perfect person, and the Son as perfect, in a perfect person, and the Holy Spirit as perfect, in a perfect person, proceeding from the Father." The Montanist said: "How is that possible? He himself says, 'I and the Father are one' (John 10:30)." The Orthodox Christian said: "He did not say, 'I am one,' but 'we are one,' so that we may know the subsistent character of the persons. But I am amazed that you remember the Gospels and yet do not walk straight toward their truth." The Montanist said: "I am persuaded by the Gospels." The Orthodox Christian said: "Then show me where it is written in the Gospels that 'I am the Father and the Son and the Spirit.'" The Montanist said: "'Whoever has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9)." The Orthodox Christian said: "Yes, the Father. He did not say that he himself is the Father, but that he is such as the Father is." The Montanist said: "Do you want to know that those who do not receive the Advocate are orphans? Listen to the Lord saying: 'It is to your advantage that I go away. If I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you. And when he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin and righteousness and judgment' (John 16:7-8). And a little later he says: 'I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you' (John 14:18). So those who have not received the Advocate are orphans." The Orthodox Christian said: "Truly, those who have not received the Advocate are not only orphans but also godless." The Montanist said: "Why then do you not receive him?" The Orthodox Christian said: "We have received him and we do receive him. But you have neither known him nor received him; rather, you have been deceived by Montanus, and with such a deception as people would not have been deceived by unless they had become vessels of the devil. For first he persuades you to say that the apostles were orphans and that the Lord Jesus was a liar when he said to them: 'I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you' (John 14:18)." The Montanist said: "We say that Christ was not in the apostles." The Orthodox Christian said: "The one who says that the Advocate was not in the apostles but in Montanus will certainly not grant that Christ was in them either. For no one can say 'Jesus is Lord' except in the Holy Spirit (1 Corinthians 12:3). And so, according to you, the apostles were orphans and the Lord Jesus Christ was a liar, while Montanus, the priest of Apollo, was truthful. What is more wretched than this deception?" The Montanist said: "We also say that the apostles had something from the Spirit, but they did not have the fullness of the Advocate." The Orthodox Christian said: "And the one who says, 'We all, with unveiled face, behold the glory of the Lord as in a mirror' (2 Corinthians 3:18)—he did not have the Spirit, but Montanus, the priest of the idol, did?" The Montanist said: "Was Paul not a persecutor?" The Orthodox Christian said: "But he became a vessel of election." The Montanist said: "And so did Montanus." The Orthodox Christian said: "But this is how the true prophet is known: he speaks the things of God. And the false prophet is known by speaking things contrary to God." The Montanist said: "And when did Montanus speak things contrary to God?" The Orthodox Christian said: "When our God and Savior says that the Advocate is another besides himself and promises to send him to the apostles, but Montanus says, 'I am the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,' it is clear that he speaks contrary to the Son and is a false prophet." The Montanist said: "We also say that the apostles had the down payment of the Spirit, but not the fullness." The Orthodox Christian said: "That the apostles were temples of the Spirit, and all the saints as well, listen to Paul saying: 'Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit within you?' (1 Corinthians 6:19) And in another place: 'You are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you' (Romans 8:9). Since there are so many testimonies saying that the Spirit was and is upon those who believe, how can you say that he was not upon the apostles?" The Montanist said: "I said that the down payment of the Spirit was in them." The Orthodox Christian said: "The Spirit himself is the down payment of the promised goods. For example, we have the promise of incorruptibility. How is it proved that we will be incorruptible? From the Spirit whom he gave us. And so we hope that every promise will be fulfilled through the presence of the Holy Spirit, so that he himself is the down payment of the promised goods."
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The Orthodox Christian is refuting the Montanist's claim that the apostles had only a partial share of the Spirit, not the fullness, by arguing that the Spirit himself is the down payment of all God's promised goods.

title: The Spirit as down payment and why women may prophesy but not write books
english: Paul says it this way: 'Now it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, who also sealed us and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts' (2 Corinthians 1:21-22). That is, we have been established with you in Christ. How do we know this? From the Spirit he has given us. For the proof of what Christ promised comes from the presence of the Spirit. He promised the kingdom of heaven; he promised incorruptibility, immortality, wisdom, sanctification, redemption. What is the proof of this gift, and where does our certainty come from? From the Spirit he has given us. For the one who has given the cause of the gifts will also give what follows from them, and for this reason the Spirit is called the down payment of the glory that is going to be revealed.

The Montanist said: 'Why do you reject the holy Maximilla and Priscilla and say that women are not permitted to prophesy? Did not Philip have four daughters who prophesied, and was not Deborah a prophetess? And does not the apostle say, "Every woman who prays or prophesies with uncovered head" (1 Corinthians 11:5)? If it is not permitted for women to prophesy, neither to pray? But if they pray, let them also prophesy.'

The Orthodox Christian said: 'We do not reject the prophecies of women. The holy Mary also prophesied, saying, "From now on all generations will call me blessed" (Luke 1:48). And as you yourself said, the holy Philip had daughters who prophesied, and Miriam the sister of Aaron prophesied. But we do not permit them to speak in the churches or to have authority over men, so as to write books in their own name. For this is to pray and prophesy with uncovered head, and so that she would not shame her head, that is, the man. Could not the holy Mary the Mother of God have written books in her own name? But she did not do so, so that she would not shame her head by having authority over men.'

The Montanist said: 'So praying or prophesying with uncovered head means not writing books?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Exactly.' The Montanist said: 'If then the holy Mary says, "From now on all generations will call me blessed," does she speak with boldness and with uncovered head, or not?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'She has a covering: the evangelist. For the gospel is not written in her name.'

The Montanist said: 'Do not take allegories as doctrines for me.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Above all, the holy Paul took allegories for the confirmation of doctrines, saying: "Abraham had two wives, which are spoken allegorically. For these are the two covenants" (Galatians 4:22, 24). But let us grant that the covering of the head is not because of allegory. Apply the allegory in all cases for me: if a woman is poor and does not have anything to cover herself with, should she not pray or prophesy?' The Montanist said: 'Can a woman be so poor that she has nothing to cover herself with?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'We have often seen women so poor that they had nothing to cover themselves with. But since you do not want there to be women so poor that they have nothing to cover themselves with, what do you do in the case of those being baptized? Should they not pray when they are baptized? And what do you say about men who often cover their heads because of hardship? Do you also forbid them to pray or prophesy?' The Montanist said: 'At that hour when she prays or prophesies, she uncovers herself.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Is he not to pray without ceasing, but to disobey the apostle who teaches him, saying, "Pray without ceasing" (1 Thessalonians 5:17)? And do you advise a woman being baptized not to pray?'

The Montanist said: 'So this is why you do not accept Priscilla and Maximilla: because they composed books.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Not only for this reason, but also because they were false prophetesses along with their leader Montanus.' The Montanist said: 'How do you know they were false prophetesses?' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Did they say the same things as Montanus?' The Montanist said: 'Yes.' The Orthodox Christian said: 'Montanus was convicted of speaking contrary to the divine Scriptures, and therefore they too will be cast out with him.'
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The Orthodox Christian has just argued that the Holy Spirit is the down payment of promised goods, and now the Montanist turns to the question of women prophesying, citing Priscilla and Maximilla.
